hook_text: One crate of tomatoes, many bottles of sauce. Why is the sauce worth so much more?
clip_script: Tzaneen, tomato country. A farmer sells a crate of tomatoes to a factory. The factory washes, cooks and mixes them with sugar, vinegar and spices, bottles the sauce, adds a label and sends it to shops. Every step adds value, so the sauce sells for much more than the tomatoes. Raw materials are usually cheap. Manufactured goods are worth more. Countries that make finished goods keep more of the money and the jobs.
visual_style: Whiteboard crate of tomatoes moving along a factory line into bottles, with a price tag growing bigger at each step.
mood: Practical and eye-opening, like following the money.
pacing: One step of the factory line per beat, each with a growing price tag, then the big lesson.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and compare the price of a raw food and a product made from it at a shop.
